Resolves #18781

`component.Abstract#parent` already ranks the owner over the render parent. The two manager traversals did not, so any component drawn outside its owner's node was invisible to a lookup from that owner: a button's menu (rendered at `document.body`), an open submenu (under the app's main view), the tab overflow control and Markdown-injected components for their whole life, and a drag proxy's content for the length of the drag. The drag case is the one that made `getReference` answer `null` mid-drag and take the Colors grid down with it (#18763).

`down()` now walks the ownership tree — each component once, however many ways the walk reaches it — and `up()` walks `parent`. **The workaround in `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs` is deleted.**

Evidence: L2 (real containers, a real `DragProxyContainer` and a real `menu.List` in the unit runtime) → L2 required (AC-1, AC-2); L3 (the served Colors app under `tearOutMatrix`, without the workaround) → L3 required (AC-4). No residual.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | `test/playwright/unit/manager/ComponentProxyTraversal.spec.mjs` › *down() from the owner reaches a component the proxy hosts* + *up() from the hosted component reaches the owner*. Red-first on `dev`: both return `null` |
| AC-2 | Two index shapes, both returned once. Same node: *down() returns a doubly reachable component once*. Two different keys: *a component rendered under the root and owned by its descendant is returned once, and still reached from its owner* — the shape `menu.List` ships for every open submenu. @neo-opus-grace's review falsifier (a real `Button` owning a real `menu.List` rendered under the root) now returns `["neo-menu-list-1"]`, where the previous head returned it twice |
| AC-3 | Measured on both revisions, interleaved — table below |
| AC-4 | `apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs` loses the construction-time resolve list, and `tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs` ran **10/10 clean** without it (pre-fix rate ~1 in 3). The app spec's arms now assert the opposite of what they asserted in #18774: the lookup **reaches** the grid while the proxy holds it |
| AC-5 | Full unit suite 4194 passed, 0 failed; component `dashboard` + `draggable` + `menu` + `tab` 175/175. The Workstation tour arms are Brain-gated e2e and sit in Post-Merge Validation |

## AC-3 — the cost

853 components, 1000 full non-matching walks per sample, `origin/dev`'s manager and this head swapped in turn in one worktree, four samples each:

| app state | `dev` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| no owned component (`ownerMap` empty) | 0.504 / 0.476 / 0.502 ms | 0.553 / 0.442 / 0.417 ms — within noise |
| one owned component (any app holding a menu) | 0.477 / 0.466 / 0.479 / 0.485 ms | 0.682 / 0.709 / 0.664 / 0.735 ms — **+46 %** |

The walk-wide dedupe is what costs. Remembering every node cost **+74 %** and was rejected; only a component with an owner can be reached twice or close a cycle, so only those are remembered, and a walk through an app without owned components pays nothing. A `parentComponent` read costs the same as a `Set` lookup (≈ 0.07 ms per 853 reads), so there was no cheaper membership test to trade for it. All 22 `down()` call sites in the engine are lookups — reference resolution, toolbar buttons, a dialog header — not per-frame work.

## Deltas from ticket

**The ticket asked for `getDirectChildren()` to widen; it must not.** `mixin.VdomLifecycle` unmounts by it (`:1022`), and `ai/client/ComponentService` answers tree questions with it — both want the render children exactly. The widening lives in `getOwnedChildren()`, which only the ownership walk calls.

**The population is permanent, not drag-scoped** — my first head documented it as "a drag proxy is the one case in the engine", and @neo-opus-grace's review showed the engine's own writers contradict that (`button/Base.mjs`, `menu/List.mjs`, `tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`, `component/Markdown.mjs`). The JSDoc and this body now name them. It also means `down()` array consumers — `ai/client/ComponentService#queryComponent` for Neural Link, `app/header/Canvas.mjs`'s per-button listeners — now see owned floating components under their owners, which is the answer `parent` already gives.

**A `parentComponent` cycle ends both walks.** #18781's Fix raised it; the visited set answers it for `down()` and `up()` alike, pinned by *a parentComponent cycle ends both walks*.

**`register()` and `unregister()` were each maintaining a reverse index by hand.** `addToIndex` / `removeFromIndex` replace all three copies.

## Test Evidence

Red-first against the previous head `77107672c9`: *a component rendered under the root and owned by its descendant is returned once* read `["neo-component-2", "neo-component-2"]`. Mutation, restored byte-identical: removing `walkDown()`'s visited guard reds the same arm (`Received length: 2`). The cycle arm is not run against a guard-less head on purpose — `up()` without it loops synchronously and would hang the worker rather than fail.

The unit-suite flake that reddened this PR's first CI run (`CrossWindowDragTarget.spec.mjs:54`, a process-global emptiness assertion) is fixed separately in #18786, merged; this branch is rebased onto it.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The Workstation tour e2e arms (`WorkstationFiveBeatNL`) are the widest `down()` consumer and need the Brain runtime; @neo-opus-vega measured `scene 4` / `scene 5` red and `scene 2` intermittent **at the branch point** today, so a run here could not attribute either way. Re-run on merged `dev` and compare against that baseline.
